clue.text: Hard slant's adopted in assembly

indicators.note: what is adopted is taken in, so the slant word absorbs the other letter

parts.note: a camber is the slight slope or tilt of a road surface
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A tough political bias has taken hold in a parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's stands for 'has': the slant has adopted H, which sits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber is a legislative body, such as the upper or lower house of a parliament.

clue.text: Nick manages to acquire skip…
… free, when retail use has been reviewed
Working in transport to get extra income

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: a bus is public transport
on means functioning, working

explanation.surface: A transit worker takes a side job to boost earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is an additional payment on top of normal wages.

clue.text: Fulminate about common idea brought up in dispatches

indicators.note: about means going round, so the anger word surrounds the other

parts.note: to fulminate is to rage

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a trope is a recurring motif or commonplace idea

explanation.surface: A war correspondent rants about a hackneyed theme raised in their reports.
explanation.definitionFit: Reportage is news reporting, the material a correspondent files in dispatches.

clue.text: Seduced by bum with dated expression

indicators.note: an expression is something spoken, so the words are to be judged by how they are voiced

parts.note: to bum is to cadge (beg for something); dated is old

explanation.surface: Someone was lured in by a layabout using old-fashioned chat-up lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' as a verb means to scrounge, as in bumming a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: To cajole is to coax or persuade someone with flattery, which is a gentle form of seduction.

clue.text: Prudent to move medical facility out of food processing plant

indicators.note: moving something out of a place takes it away, so letters are removed

parts.note: a cannery is a factory where food is canned
ER is the emergency room of a hospital

explanation.surface: Relocating a clinic away from a food factory is the sensible choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Canny means shrewd and careful, especially with money, a close synonym of prudent.

clue.text: Occasional jade auction held in strange city

indicators.note: occasional means only now and then, so just a few letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters only

indicators.note: something held in another sits inside it

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd
an auction is a type of sale

explanation.surface: A one-off sale of jade goes under the hammer in an exotic town.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerusalem is the ancient holy city in the Middle East.

clue.text: French journal removes depleted database — it's a dud
Writer talked about devil

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Victorian novelist Charles
second meaning: a mild euphemism for the devil in speech

explanation.walkthrough: 'Talked about' reads like a sound signal, but it qualifies the second definition: the word replaces devil in spoken exclamations.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist's surname doubles as an old exclamatory substitute for the devil.

clue.text: Central shipyard allows owner to build tower

indicators.note: central asks for only the middle letters of each following word

parts.note: the two middle letters of this eight-letter word
the two middle letters of this six-letter word
the single middle letter of this five-letter word

explanation.surface: A shipyard's proprietor gets permission to put up a tower on the site.
explanation.definitionFit: A pylon is a tall steel lattice tower carrying electricity cables.

clue.text: Roam around in alarm, taking everything in

indicators.note: to roam around is to wander about, so these letters are moved about too
in places the wandered letters inside the word for alarm

parts.note: panic is sudden alarm
its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wanders about in a fright, eyes darting everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A panoramic view takes in the whole scene, an unbroken wide sweep of everything around.

clue.text: A solution for stiff locks

parts.note: surface reading: a lubricant or fix for door locks that are hard to turn
setter's reading: a liquid sprayed to keep hair (locks) stiff in place

explanation.walkthrough: 'Solution' means a liquid, not an answer, and 'locks' are tresses, not door fittings; 'stiff' describes the result, not the problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair spray is a lacquer solution applied to hold a hairstyle rigidly in place.

clue.text: Reason poles are found in a place like York?

indicators.note: things found in something sit within it

parts.note: York is a see, the seat of an archbishop
the north and south poles, N and S

explanation.surface: A question about whether there's any logic to finding poles in York.
explanation.walkthrough: York is an archbishop's see, a diocese seat; 'a place like' tells you York is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason and sense both mean sound judgement or rationality, as in 'talk some sense'.

clue.text: Rich people like us seldom have starters

indicators.note: starters are the first parts, so only each word's opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A self-deprecating remark that ordinary folk rarely eat first courses.
explanation.definitionFit: Plush describes something luxurious and expensive-looking, a synonym of rich in furnishings.

clue.text: Ripped up shores with tool that's used to protect mounts

indicators.note: something ripped up is torn apart, so its letters are scattered and rebuilt

parts.note: its letters rearranged
a hoe is a garden tool

explanation.surface: Coastal defences torn up by a digging implement used to protect hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseshoe is a U-shaped iron plate nailed to a hoof to protect a riding animal's feet.

clue.text: Rugby side required to score 147?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the New Zealand national rugby union team
second meaning: a 147 maximum break in snooker means potting a black after every red

explanation.walkthrough: In snooker, the maximum break of 147 needs all fifteen reds each followed by the black (worth seven), then the remaining colours.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Zealand team wears black kit, and a perfect snooker break demands every black be potted.

clue.text: Tool for cutting plank supporting small part of raised concrete

indicators.note: in a down clue, a support sits underneath, so the plank comes after the rest
in a down clue, raised means lifted to read from bottom to top
being part of something means sitting within it

parts.note: concrete means real, tangible
S is the abbreviation for small
a beam is a long piece of timber

explanation.surface: Building-site talk: a saw for a plank holding up a lifted slab of concrete.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' puts the plank beneath the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser beam is a concentrated light beam that can slice through metal and other materials.

clue.text: Check on old company behind confectionery

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
O is the abbreviation for old
Co is short for company
behind schedule means late

explanation.surface: An inspection of a long-established firm lagging behind in sweet-making.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate is a sweet treat, one of the main kinds of confectionery.

clue.text: Difficulty getting to the top for unqualified head

parts.note: sheer means absolute, without qualification, as in sheer nonsense
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: An untrained boss struggles to climb the career ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheerness is also a town in Kent, but here the word is read as the quality of being sheer, that is steep.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheerness is steepness, the near-vertical slope that makes reaching a summit hard.

clue.text: Amount political party initially tucked inside secret location

indicators.note: inside places the party and letter within the amount

parts.note: a sum is an amount
the African National Congress of South Africa

indicators.note: initially points to only the opening letter of the word

parts.note: the opening letter only

explanation.surface: Cash a party first hid away somewhere secret.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctum is a private, secluded inner room where someone retreats undisturbed.

clue.text: Low rubbish describing heavy fellow's chest

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
BS is short for bullshit, nonsense

explanation.surface: A cheap jibe mocking an overweight man's physique.
explanation.walkthrough: MOOBS is British slang for 'man boobs', the fatty chest of an overweight man.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang term names breast-like fat on a man's chest, so it fits a heavy fellow.

clue.text: Provider, when I will have gone, becomes more flexible

indicators.note: something that has gone is no longer there, so that letter drops out

parts.note: a supplier provides goods
taken as written

explanation.surface: A supplier becomes more accommodating once I'm out of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Suppler is the comparative of supple, meaning bending easily.

clue.text: Manicheism provides a comfortable place to be

indicators.note: the long word provides, that is supplies from within itself, a run of letters

parts.note: letters three to seven of this word

explanation.surface: A believer finds a dualist religion a cosy spiritual home.
explanation.walkthrough: Manicheism is an ancient dualist religion of light versus darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a position or role where someone fits snugly and feels at ease.

clue.text: Trough offering shelter in church

indicators.note: in places the shelter inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a hut is a simple shelter

explanation.surface: A feeding trough set up as a refuge inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A chute is a sloping channel or trough down which things slide.

clue.text: Cleaner gets sick pensioner to eat nothing

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the other letters go round the zero

parts.note: barfs is slang for vomits
OAP is an old age pensioner
O is the zero shape

explanation.surface: A household help falls ill when an elderly client refuses food.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar of soap is a block of the stuff people wash with, a cleaner in the literal sense.

clue.text: Wager about gold in Australia, is outstanding

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the bet goes around the metal

parts.note: a bet is a wager
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A bet on gold prices Down Under is still unpaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' suggests owing, but it means excellent; 'in Australia' flags the slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaut is Australian slang for something excellent, short for beauty.

clue.text: Regularly offer eldest some meals

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Advice to routinely give the oldest child a few dinners.
explanation.definitionFit: A feed is a meal, especially a large one or one given to a baby or animal.

clue.text: Move stand, then reconnect

parts.note: to touch is to move emotionally
a base is a stand that something rests on

explanation.surface: Instructions to shift a display stand and then plug it back in.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch base is an idiom for getting back in contact with someone briefly.

clue.text: Message William expects to be partially rejected

indicators.note: rejected suggests thrown back, so the letters are read from right to left
partially means only part of the run of letters is used

parts.note: the end of the first name and start of the second word

explanation.surface: A note that William anticipates will be turned down in part.
explanation.definitionFit: An email is an electronic message sent between computers.

clue.text: Teams we organised are best, some say

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A boast that the sides we arranged are top class, according to some.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some say' marks the definition as slang: in Cockney rhyming slang Mae West, the film star, rhymes with best.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang replaces a word with a phrase that rhymes with it, so the actress's name stands for best.

clue.text: Erroneously pick up note by quiet listener

parts.note: mi is a note in the sol-fa scale
sh is a call for quiet
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly collects a message left by a discreet eavesdropper.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up can mean to catch a sound, so getting it wrong is to mishear.
